title: Rubio Says US Will Discuss Venezuelan Crude Refining With Reliance in India
excerpt: In Mumbai, Marco Rubio called India a refining superpower, praised its progress diversifying away from Russian oil, and flagged sanctions as an obstacle to work through.
body:
• U.S. Secretary of State Marco Rubio said on October 20 in Mumbai that the United States will talk with Reliance about refining more Venezuelan crude and about producing oil in Venezuela.
  • Rubio called India a refining superpower because it can refine heavy crude, and said India has pre-existing oil concessions in Venezuela that could produce more.
  • He said India had made substantial progress diversifying its energy supplies away from Russia, while noting sanctions are among the impediments that still have to be worked through.
  • For energy buyers and fuel users, no agreement was announced on Tuesday; the next concrete step is Rubio's planned trip on Wednesday to Reliance's Jamnagar refinery.

The United States will discuss refining more Venezuelan crude with Reliance, U.S. Secretary of State Marco Rubio said in Mumbai on Tuesday (October 20, 2026), at the start of his India trip. Rubio also said the U.S. delegation would discuss producing oil in Venezuela with Reliance, The Hindu reported.

https://x.com/MeghUpdates/status/2112501451209703689

Asked what role India can play in meeting world energy demand, Rubio pointed to the scale and type of India's refining capacity.

"India is a refining superpower. They have the capability to refine heavy crude. They've done so in the past, and I think as more and more Venezuelan oil comes online, it's something they can do."

— Marco Rubio, U.S. Secretary of State

Rubio added that India also has pre-existing oil concessions in Venezuela that can produce more itself. He did not present Venezuelan supply as a complete replacement for any shortfall elsewhere. He said he was not claiming Venezuela alone could fill the hole that could be caused by some of the things happening around the world, but that over time it could, and in the short term it could help.

On Wednesday (October 21, 2026), Rubio is due to travel from Mumbai to Jamnagar to see the Reliance energy refinery and the Vantara animal facility, in a visit hosted by the Ambani family that officials termed a private visit, The Hindu said. Reliance runs the world's largest refining complex at Jamnagar, and its chairman is Mukesh Ambani, according to Hindu BusinessLine. That stop puts the refining discussion at the plant itself rather than leaving it as a statement made in Mumbai.

The second part of Rubio's energy message concerned Russia. He said India had made substantial progress in diversifying its energy supplies, including away from its key importer Russia, in the wording used by The Hindu, and he repeated India's own stated position.

"What India has expressed repeatedly is their desire to diversify their energy portfolio, which is a smart thing to do."

— Marco Rubio, U.S. Secretary of State

Rubio added that this was not easy to do from one day to the next, and that the United States was happy to see the progress. Hindu BusinessLine, reporting the same remarks, said Rubio described diversifying oil purchases as a smart thing to do and said India sounded ready and willing on Venezuelan oil. He also flagged the obstacle in the same remarks: there might be a few impediments in the way in terms of sanctions and so forth that would have to be worked through.

The context is India's dependence on imported crude and its continuing purchases from Russia. Hindu BusinessLine reported that India imports more than 85% of its crude oil requirements, that India still buys millions of barrels of Russian oil every day, and that India stands second, after China, on a list of the top five importers of Russian oil referred to in U.S. legislation signed in September. That legislation authorises tariffs of up to 100% on those importers, but President Donald Trump waived its substantive provisions last Friday, a decision Rubio has said was influenced in part by the effort to finalise a trade deal.

For Indian refiners, the question raised on Tuesday is practical rather than rhetorical. Venezuelan crude is heavy crude, and Rubio's case rests on India's demonstrated ability to process it. Whether more of it actually flows to Jamnagar depends on the sanctions issues he named, on Venezuelan oil coming online in greater volume, and on what Reliance agrees to in the discussions he announced.

No volumes, timelines or commercial terms were given in the remarks reported on Tuesday. The next test of the proposal is the Jamnagar visit on Wednesday, after which any statement from Reliance or from the U.S. delegation about refining volumes or Venezuelan production would show whether the Mumbai remarks have moved into a specific plan.
